content: 1. Digoxin levels are increased by the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering drugs that affect this pathway. 2. Atropine increases digoxin levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with IV/IM administration. 3. Azithromycin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Aztreonam increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Benazepril increases digoxin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Bendroflumethiazide enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs affect serum potassium levels, with digoxin increasing and bendroflumethiazide decreasing potassium. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 7. Berotralstat increases digoxin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely and consider dose adjustments for P-gp substrates when co-administered. 8. Betaxolol enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. The combination may increase the risk of bradycardia. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Bisoprolol enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergism. Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. The combination may increase the risk of bradycardia. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Bosutinib increases digoxin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Bremelanotide decreases digoxin levels or effects by slowing gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications. Avoid use with oral drugs dependent on threshold concentrations for efficacy. 12. Bretylium increases digoxin toxicity through sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, including elevated blood pressure and heart rate. Avoid simultaneous initiation of therapy with digitalis glycosides and bretylium. Bretylium is contraindicated for digoxin-induced arrhythmias. 13. Brimonidine enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Bumetanide enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergism. Digoxin increases and bumetanide decreases serum potassium levels. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 15. Bupropion decreases digoxin levels or effects, potentially by inducing the OATP4C1 transporter involved in digoxin renal elimination. Monitor for reduced digoxin concentrations and adjust therapy as needed. 16. Calcifediol may cause hypercalcemia, increasing the risk of digoxin toxicity. Monitor serum calcium levels and observe for signs of digoxin toxicity. 17. Calcium acetate enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Calcium carbonate increases digoxin levels or effects by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Candesartan and digoxin both increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 24.
